Comments (English): [ Quiet and Great Cleaning, Not-so-great rack layout ] || ---------------- || I love how quiet it is compared to my last dishwasher, and it does a great job of cleaning. The silverware racks were also hard to secure, and we had to use a twist tie to keep one of them in place and not rattling around a bit. Sentence (English): In addition to the 6-person one I was using, I ended up getting a mini one.
Comments (English): [ It's so convenient and great for a single-person household ] || ---------------- || In addition to the 6-person one I was using, I ended up getting a mini one. Even though it's mini, it's small and compact. It's definitely on the small side, so I can put it away without feeling burdened, and it's really packed with features, so I use it more often than the 6-person one. For reference, I live alone and I only cook simple dinners on weekdays, so I don't usually have a lot of dishes to wash. Once I get hooked, I cook hard and sometimes I make a lot of dishes, but it's not that often, so I really wanted a mini like this. When I came home from work, I always had less time, and I would waste time washing dishes and get a little tired, but now that I have some free time, I'm really happy. It's optimized for 2-3 person households, so if you don't like bulky appliances and often wash dishes, this will be helpful. I'll organize my user reviews in detail. *Delivery and installation It was packed in thick Styrofoam to prevent damage during delivery, so the delivery box was a bit big, but it was easy to bring it into the house because it was wrapped with string. The delivery box felt a bit heavy, but when I actually took it out and moved it, it was moderately heavy and I could carry it by myself. It was okay to move. It is a simple, no-installation product that does not require an installation process, so you just need to attach the drain hose and set the position. Since the water supply hose is included, I thought automatic water supply might be possible. I can no longer pull out the line under the sink, so I am using it with manual water supply. It is very easy to install when using manual water supply, which is good. *Operation method: Turn on the power first and pour water into the upper part until you hear a beep. It is said to hold about 5 liters, but if you fill the water tank that is delivered with it and pour it through the water supply drip tray, it will go in well without spilling around. After that, select the menu and press the operation button right away, and it will work well. Before operation, the dishes are sprayed with strong water from the bottom, so you should turn them over so that they face downwards as much as possible. It is sprayed from the top, but the bottom is wider, so it is very helpful to turn them over. It automatically washes with high-temperature water at 72 degrees and dries them smartly. The drying function is really convenient and good. After operation is complete, the drying function turns on and off repeatedly with the timer function, so if you do not want it, you can open the door after completion when it is dry to some extent. *Function The little guy has quite a variety of functions. The menu is more diverse than I thought, and it is fun to look at because it has a transparent window. It has a steam sterilization function, and it is very convenient because it handles drying and storage functions after washing with the air circulation full drying system. The fan inside the device operates continuously for 72 hours by repeating operation and rest after completion, so it can dry and store dishes cleanly without any smell, so it can be used as a dish drying rack. Although it is small, it has two stages in the upper and lower parts, 9 high temperature, high pressure, and 360-degree water spray, so it washes every corner well. I put it in with the red grease, and it was washed off perfectly. I put it back in after removing only the large debris. It is good because it can be washed at high temperature for 30 minutes with the steam function, so I can use dishes that are clean and sparkling more pleasantly. Among the standard, strong, eco, quick, and steam functions, I often use strong. I used the dishwasher detergent that I was using before, so I used that. I split it into 1/4, but it felt a bit too much, so I thought I should reduce the amount of detergent. I think it would be good if it was easy to control even though it was a powder detergent that you pour. I think it would be good if it was easy to control even though it was a powder detergent that you pour. It washes away even the oil well and dries, so I use it well every day because it does its job well! Sentence (English): When I came home from work, I always had less time, and I would waste time washing dishes and get a little tired, but now that I have some free time, I'm really happy.

It is a simple, no-installation product that does not require an installation process, so you just need to attach the drain hose and set the position. Since the water supply hose is included, I thought automatic water supply might be possible. I can no longer pull out the line under the sink, so I am using it with manual water supply. It is very easy to install when using manual water supply, which is good. *Operation method: Turn on the power first and pour water into the upper part until you hear a beep. It is said to hold about 5 liters, but if you fill the water tank that is delivered with it and pour it through the water supply drip tray, it will go in well without spilling around. After that, select the menu and press the operation button right away, and it will work well. Before operation, the dishes are sprayed with strong water from the bottom, so you should turn them over so that they face downwards as much as possible. It is sprayed from the top, but the bottom is wider, so it is very helpful to turn them over. It automatically washes with high-temperature water at 72 degrees and dries them smartly. The drying function is really convenient and good. After operation is complete, the drying function turns on and off repeatedly with the timer function, so if you do not want it, you can open the door after completion when it is dry to some extent. *Function The little guy has quite a variety of functions. The menu is more diverse than I thought, and it is fun to look at because it has a transparent window. It has a steam sterilization function, and it is very convenient because it handles drying and storage functions after washing with the air circulation full drying system. The fan inside the device operates continuously for 72 hours by repeating operation and rest after completion, so it can dry and store dishes cleanly without any smell, so it can be used as a dish drying rack. Although it is small, it has two stages in the upper and lower parts, 9 high temperature, high pressure, and 360-degree water spray, so it washes every corner well. I put it in with the red grease, and it was washed off perfectly. I put it back in after removing only the large debris. It is good because it can be washed at high temperature for 30 minutes with the steam function, so I can use dishes that are clean and sparkling more pleasantly. Among the standard, strong, eco, quick, and steam functions, I often use strong. I used the dishwasher detergent that I was using before, so I used that. I split it into 1/4, but it felt a bit too much, so I thought I should reduce the amount of detergent. I think it would be good if it was easy to control even though it was a powder detergent that you pour. It washes away even the oil well and dries, so I use it well every day because it does its job well! I split it into 1/4, but it felt a bit too much, so I thought I should reduce the amount of detergent. I think it would be good if it was easy to control even though it was a powder detergent that you pour. It washes away even the oil well and dries, so I use it well every day because it does its job well! It washes away even the oil well and dries, so I use it well every day because it does its job well! It washes away even the oil well and dries, so I use it well every day because it does its job well! Comments (English): [ It's so convenient and great for a single-person household ] || ---------------- || In addition to the 6-person one I was using, I ended up getting a mini one. It's definitely on the small side, so I can put it away without feeling burdened, and it's really packed with features, so I use it more often than the 6-person one. For reference, I live alone and I only cook simple dinners on weekdays, so I don't usually have a lot of dishes to wash. Once I get hooked, I cook hard and sometimes I make a lot of dishes, but it's not that often, so I really wanted a mini like this. I'll organize my user reviews in detail. *Delivery and installation It was packed in thick Styrofoam to prevent damage during delivery, so the delivery box was a bit big, but it was easy to bring it into the house because it was wrapped with string. The delivery box felt a bit heavy, but when I actually took it out and moved it, it was moderately heavy and I could carry it by myself. It was okay to move. It is a simple, no-installation product that does not require an installation process, so you just need to attach the drain hose and set the position. Since the water supply hose is included, I thought automatic water supply might be possible. I can no longer pull out the line under the sink, so I am using it with manual water supply. It is very easy to install when using manual water supply, which is good. *Operation method: Turn on the power first and pour water into the upper part until you hear a beep. It is said to hold about 5 liters, but if you fill the water tank that is delivered with it and pour it through the water supply drip tray, it will go in well without spilling around. After that, select the menu and press the operation button right away, and it will work well. Before operation, the dishes are sprayed with strong water from the bottom, so you should turn them over so that they face downwards as much as possible. It is sprayed from the top, but the bottom is wider, so it is very helpful to turn them over. It automatically washes with high-temperature water at 72 degrees and dries them smartly. The drying function is really convenient and good. After operation is complete, the drying function turns on and off repeatedly with the timer function, so if you do not want it, you can open the door after completion when it is dry to some extent. *Function The little guy has quite a variety of functions. The menu is more diverse than I thought, and it is fun to look at because it has a transparent window. It has a steam sterilization function, and it is very convenient because it handles drying and storage functions after washing with the air circulation full drying system. The fan inside the device operates continuously for 72 hours by repeating operation and rest after completion, so it can dry and store dishes cleanly without any smell, so it can be used as a dish drying rack. Although it is small, it has two stages in the upper and lower parts, 9 high temperature, high pressure, and 360-degree water spray, so it washes every corner well. I put it in with the red grease, and it was washed off perfectly. I put it back in after removing only the large debris. It is good because it can be washed at high temperature for 30 minutes with the steam function, so I can use dishes that are clean and sparkling more pleasantly. Among the standard, strong, eco, quick, and steam functions, I often use strong. I used the dishwasher detergent that I was using before, so I used that. I split it into 1/4, but it felt a bit too much, so I thought I should reduce the amount of detergent. I think it would be good if it was easy to control even though it was a powder detergent that you pour. It washes away even the oil well and dries, so I use it well every day because it does its job well! This dishwasher is defective-has never worked, and has required multiple repairs, and is still unusable. Sentence (English): We have owned three Bosch dishwasher's in the past 30 years.
Comments (English): [ Bosch is always great! ] || ---------------- || We have owned three Bosch dishwasher's in the past 30 years. Our last one died after about 10 years. To replace it, I wanted a 500 series but it wasn't available in black. We only could get the 100 series, that was on the low end of what we wanted. Now that we are using it- we are very happy. It washes dishes well on the auto setting, drying is fine and at 48 decibels is quite enough. Looks like the higher end models have useless features. The 100 series doesn't have all stainless interior, who cares? The interior is just fine. Higher end series are quieter but the 100 series is fine. Lastly how many people need additional settings like the crystal mode. Over all it is an excellent dishwasher for the cost. Spending more money isn't worth it.

Sentence (English): I love how quiet this dishwasher is!

I ended up removing the top rack on that one because there wasn't enough room for everything, even when I adjusted the 2nd rack height. I have not had to do so with this dishwasher. I am really happy with this purchase!

Sentence (English): This dishwasher is as basic as it gets, but in the short time we've had it, it does what it's supposed to do - wash dishes pretty well.
Comments (English): [ It washes dishes. ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher is as basic as it gets, but in the short time we've had it, it does what it's supposed to do - wash dishes pretty well. There's nothing fancy or trendy about it. It doesn't connect to an app, it doesn't access the internet, there's no stainless steel inside, and I doubt it'll scrub your stainless steel pans. If you want a simple dishwasher that does what it's told, this may be a good choice. The last two, more expensive dishwashers we had from other brands didn't last long (the more recent one only two years) so we went with the basics. As I understand it, more expensive dishwashers have more features, so there are more things to break, and they don't last longer than less expensive models. Based on our experience we bought an extended warranty. We paid, I think, $120 to cover the previous dish washer and after a second break down in two years we were paid the purchase price to buy a new one. If it's out of warranty we'd have to pay a repair tech $100-$150 just to come to our house.

Sentence (English): Please note this review is nothing against Home Depot where I purchased this dishwasher but rather the product itself.
Comments (English): [ Dishes don't get clean ] || ---------------- || Please note this review is nothing against Home Depot where I purchased this dishwasher but rather the product itself. I did research before buying this unit and saw all the rave reviews for it. So I bought this dishwasher and have owned it now for about a month. During that time, and we have a very large family, we ran the dishwasher twice a day. The silverware most notably doesn't get clean, specifically if you have avocado or peanut butter, anything that's remotely sticky, you have to wash the silverware first and get even the slightest film off or this dishwasher will not clean it. I have tried all the different cycles, and I get the same result. Just my opinion, look elsewhere unless you want to rinse clean every single thing you're putting in the dishwasher and then run the cycle. I use high-quality dishwasher tabs as well as a rinse aid liquid as needed. The only pro that I can list about this unit is that it is quiet when it runs.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher is great but the installation was a nightmare.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher is great, but……….  ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher is great but the installation was a nightmare. The installer had no idea how to install it: it was crooked, the whole dishwasher moved when opening and closing the door, the controls on top of the door were completely exposed and not hidden as designed, I could put all of my fingers between the countertop and the top of the dishwasher, the rubber piece at the bottom of the door was hanging out and no kick plate was installed, the drain tubing to the garbage disposal was installed incorrectly, etc. I called Costco and told them some of my concerns. They had the installation company come back out. They were going to send the same installer so I had to tell them to send a different installer. The new installer came to check out my claims and pretty much ended up uninstalling it and starting over. There were pieces missing: the brackets that hold the dishwasher from falling forward when opening the door and a few pieces for installing the kick plate. The second installer, who was great, found some clips from another install and used them on my dishwasher to hold it in until we get the correct parts. He replumbed it, centered it and pushed it back so the control panel was hidden. I'm now waiting to get replacement parts or another dishwasher. I'm hoping for another dishwasher because I want to know that I have all of the correct parts and that this expensive and beautifully designed dishwasher won't fail before it's time due to damage from improper installation and missing or incorrect replacement parts. I will update this review once I hear back from Costco and let you all know if they're going to get replacement parts or a new dishwasher. I gave this product five stars because it appears to be very well made. I wish Costco let us rate the installation and the product, separately. Side note: I found out that the first installer was a new employee. Apparently, his training didn't take.

We replaced an older LG dishwasher with this GE unit. The top buttons on this unit are a bit awkward as I found that I need to roll my fingers a bit in order to find the activation spot. Not a big deal, but worth mentioning. The trays feel like they aren't even meant to fit this machine. The top tray wiggles, moves around and doesn't glide smoothly, and the rails are a bit flimsy. The bottom tray feels similar, except it's the rollers that feel loose. Our old LG had a similar setup, and both trays would glide in and out with minimal effort, and they just felt sturdy. We bought this online and didn't get to check it out in a store first or else I'm sure we would have noticed this. It's a shame that manufacturers are cutting costs wherever they can instead of making a quality product. We found that the only way that this unit will leave plastic wear dry is by using the dry boost function. We had originally left this turned off as the Normal wash cycle was 78 minutes, which seemed great. When opening the unit after this cycle, almost everything inside was very wet (the utensils were dry, but water ran off the bottom of the rack when we picked it up). It seems like units that do not have a heated dry cycle are like this. With the Dry Boost function turned on, the overall wash/dry time increased to either 120 or 180 minutes, depending on which level you choose. At the 120 mark, the dishes (plastics) are about as dry as they would have been with our old LG unit. At 180 they were almost completely dry.

Sentence (English): (This review was collected as part of a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ First time use - It doesn't work ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) I'm just moving into a new place, and decided to try my new Bosch SHPM98W75N/20 to wash my newly unpacked dishes. I noticed that there were water droplet marks inside the door of the dishwaher, as if it had been used, but I thought maybe it had been factory tested or something. thought nothing of it. Only one dish was dirty, had some dressing from eating a salad on it, the others had been packed clean. Just wanted them fresh before putting them into the kitchen cupboards. Wow, what a disappointment. First, I noticed that the "Auto" cycle selection light worked, but the "Sanitize" setting didn't light. Started it anyway. Was happy to hear almost nothing, as advertised - a very quiet operation. However, after a time, the red light turned off, and I went to open the washer. There was a E-15 code, and my dishes were dripping wet and cold. I re-closed the washer, thinking it just hadn't finished its cycle. But it kept running on and on. for over an hour more. I couldn't turn off the machine, and finally cut off the power with circuit breakers. (later, I unplugged it entirely) My dishes were wet, the detergent pellet was almost intact, and my dishes were covered in a light film which I guess was the salad dressing's oil all over the place. And there was a smell like old food coming from the inside. you know that smell of old, used dishwashers. I am aghast. After all the trouble of moving and of finally finding one of these dishwashers in stock, I have apparently gotten a lemon. I couldn't even take a bath to relax, because it had drained my hot water tank. I couldn't feel more disappointed and defeated. Had to give it a one star rating, because the site doesn't accept zeroes.

Sentence (English): First of all, I decided to buy this M10 after reading Youtun’s evaluation.
Comments (English): First of all, I decided to buy this M10 after reading Youtun’s evaluation. The reasons are as follows: 1. Desktop, no installation, no tee connection, manual water addition is an advantage for me, 5L can be filled up. 2. According to some evaluation results, M10 has a relatively large advantage in saving water and electricity. It also has ultra-fast washing within 30 minutes and standard washing in 1 hour and 20 minutes, which has advantages over other brands. 3. Small and exquisite. Although not too much, it is enough for a small family. Second, so far, washed 3 times. For the first time, I used a super fast wash after opening the box, mainly to test the machine. Although there are few bowls, the washing is still slightly flawed, and I can only give 80 points, but the glass pot lid is washed very clean. The second time, I used the standard washing method, and the porridge spoon on the upper layer still had sticky matter. The overall score was 85, which was better than the first time. It may be due to the long washing time and the high water temperature. The third time, I still used standard washing, put the dishwasher in the expected position, and then bought an extension tube on the next platform, put it on directly, and the washing effect was satisfactory, and I gave it 90 points. Let me talk about the disadvantages: 1. Since there is no drying function, I asked the customer service and said that this product is stored in cold air to prevent bacteria. 2. The original drainage pipe is a bit short, so it is more manufacturable
Comments (Original): 首先，看了有调测评后决定买这款M10，原因有以下几点:1、台式，免安装，免接三通，手动加水对我来说是优势，5L加满即可。2、根据有点测评结果来看，M10优势比较大，省水省电，也有超快速洗30分钟内，标准洗1小时20分，比其他品牌有优势。3、小巧。虽然装不太多，但足够小家庭使用。其次，到目前为止，洗了3次。第一次，是开箱后用超快速洗，主要是测试机器。虽然碗少，但洗还是略有瑕疵，只能给80分，但玻璃锅盖洗得挺干净。第二次，用标准洗，还是放在上层的粥勺有黏物，总体评分85，比第一次好，可能是洗的时间久和水温高有关系。第三次，还是用标准洗，把洗碗机放在预想的位置，然后在隔壁平台买了延长管，直接套上，洗碗效果满意，给90分。说下缺点:1、由于没有烘干功能，问了客服说这款是冷风抑菌保存，洗好后机器里湿湿的，为了节省时间和电费，就把碗筷拿出来，把电源关掉，让机器自己通风吹干，得这样比较好。2、原装的排水管有点短，可造性较

There is a mechanism that blows air across the dishes for 10-20 minutes. Conceptually, it makes sense. Less humidity should equal faster drying time. This particular dish washer does not have a heating element in the base of the tub. The plates and silverware dry adequately because they are loaded vertically. The bowls, pots and any other dome shaped cookware may not dry on the upward facing portion. We found that they dry faster if we remove them from the dishwasher and place them in an old fashion dish rack. Definitely not what we expected. It has been recommended that buy some special "Rinse Dry" detergent. We are not interested. We've tried several setting for the past month. We will return this dishwasher this week. We will seek another dishwasher that has an actual heating element that completely dries the dishes. My previous dishwasher was a 44db model that cost $100 more. It was a different brand. Sentence (English): This is the second KitchenAid dishwasher I've purchased in the past 6 years (two different kitchens).
Comments (English): [ Excellent Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This is the second KitchenAid dishwasher I've purchased in the past 6 years (two different kitchens). Super happy with how well this thing cleans and how quiet it is. The third rack is a game changer and significantly adds to how much you can fit into a full load. Overall build quality and look is sleek and high quality. The downside: it has LONG run cycles (2.45 hours for the last load we ran), though there are setting and wash modes to bring this down slightly. Last minor complaint, the racks leak water after a full dry, to the point where if you open the washer door all the way and extend the racks immediately after a wash cycle you'll get water on your floor. Seems like a poor design oversight on an otherwise exceptional washer. Overall still very pleased with this purchase. Huge upgrade for us over our aging Kenmore.

Sentence (English): We spent 2 months researching which dishwasher to purchase after our older Kenmore Elite bit the dust.
Comments (English): [ After all the research. Bosch 500 ] || ---------------- || We spent 2 months researching which dishwasher to purchase after our older Kenmore Elite bit the dust. We decided on the Bosch 500 Series (SHPM65Z52N) and although it's only been installed for a couple of days we are very pleased so far. Drying performance was a BIG concern for us since many reviewers indicated the drying on these was poor. I'm not sure where that comes from, but ours drys just as well as our old Kenmore which had a heating element in the bottom. We use the rinse aid, and we always set it so the door opens when it's done and most dishes are dried just fine. Oh sure there may be a couple items where water has pooled-up and is therefore not dry, but it's common sense that not all pooled water will be completely dried. So, so far we are thrilled with drying performance! As far as cleaning performance, we haven't put any really nasty baked-on dishes in there, so we can't speak to that just yet, but if it's as good as as our 20-year old Kenmore it'll be just fine. We LOVE the 3rd rack and all the different was to configure the racks to suit the current load of dishes. The only thing that concerns me is, when I was doing two test loads on the Speed 60 setting to ensure there were no leaks, the sides and especially the back got quite hot. In fact using an Ideal 61-340 multimeter with temperature probe the back of the dishwasher got up to about 148 degrees. Which in and of itself is not a huge concern, but the concern is that with the back of the machine being really close to an exterior wall up here in northern Wisconsin where the walls get fairly cold (not much insulation in the walls) will that machine's heat cause condensation on the wall thus encouraging mildew or rot? I guess I won't know unless I pull the machine out immediately after a cycle. But so far, we are VERY happy that we went with a Bosch 500!

Sentence (English): We spent 2 months researching which dishwasher to purchase after our older Kenmore Elite bit the dust.
Comments (English): [ After all the research. Bosch 500 ] || ---------------- || We spent 2 months researching which dishwasher to purchase after our older Kenmore Elite bit the dust. We decided on the Bosch 500 Series (SHPM65Z52N) and although it's only been installed for a couple of days we are very pleased so far. Drying performance was a BIG concern for us since many reviewers indicated the drying on these was poor. I'm not sure where that comes from, but ours drys just as well as our old Kenmore which had a heating element in the bottom. We use the rinse aid, and we always set it so the door opens when it's done and most dishes are dried just fine. Oh sure there may be a couple items where water has pooled-up and is therefore not dry, but it's common sense that not all pooled water will be completely dried. So, so far we are thrilled with drying performance! As far as cleaning performance, we haven't put any really nasty baked-on dishes in there, so we can't speak to that just yet, but if it's as good as as our 20-year old Kenmore it'll be just fine. We LOVE the 3rd rack and all the different was to configure the racks to suit the current load of dishes.The only thing that concerns me is, when I was doing two test loads on the Speed 60 setting to ensure there were no leaks, the sides and especially the back got quite hot. In fact using an Ideal 61-340 multimeter with temperature probe the back of the dishwasher got up to about 148 degrees. Which in and of itself is not a huge concern, but the concern is that with the back of the machine being really close to an exterior wall up here in northern Wisconsin where the walls get fairly cold (not much insulation in the walls) will that machine's heat cause condensation on the wall thus encouraging mildew or rot? I guess I won't know unless I pull the machine out immediately after a cycle. But so far, we are VERY happy that we went with a Bosch 500!

Comments (English): [ A dishwasher with great value for money but also great performance! ] || ---------------- || I used to use this dishwasher all the time while studying abroad in the US, and this time, I discovered a dishwasher that was incredibly cost-effective. First off, the delivery/installation technician contacted me the next day after I ordered, requested photos of the installation location, and sent them to me. I was worried about installation delays because it was in the countryside, but thankfully, they installed it as quickly as possible to fit my schedule and were incredibly friendly. Depending on your kitchen setup, you may incur a small installation fee. We installed a built-in unit, and there was some construction work involved, so we ended up paying around 30,000 won. However, they installed it quickly and even gave me a quick demonstration of the product while explaining the process. The product quality is so high-quality, and my mom spends all day lounging around in front of the dishwasher. First of all, I was very satisfied with the smooth installation. Of course, installation alone isn't enough. I tried it right after dinner. 1. It saves time. First of all, I love it. I can use the dishwasher to do other things after I've finished using it, which is great. My mom is the most satisfied! 2. Using the dishwasher actually minimizes water consumption, right? It's more efficient and environmentally friendly than washing dishes by hand! I tried it after making galbijjim (braised short ribs) and the grease was removed very well! 3. Washing at high temperatures feels much more hygienic. The door automatically opens after washing, allowing for air drying. 4. The stainless steel interior is a plus! It feels clean and hygienic. 5. It's not too noisy. I can run it in the kitchen and watch TV in the living room, and I can't hear it! In fact, I can hear it the whole time. 6. I love the variety of modes. I only used it for 90 minutes, but there are seven different modes! And I love that it's height-adjustable. The user manual is also very well-written, so I plan to use it as I learn more. Above all, this spec for this price is crazy! It's such a great buy, everyone, get it!

Sentence (English): I used to use this dishwasher all the time while studying abroad in the US, and this time, I discovered a dishwasher that was incredibly cost-effective.
Comments (English): [ A dishwasher with great value for money but also great performance! ] || ---------------- || I used to use this dishwasher all the time while studying abroad in the US, and this time, I discovered a dishwasher that was incredibly cost-effective. After thorough research, I decided to buy it. I don't usually leave reviews, but this one was so good I couldn't keep it to myself! The Media brand was unfamiliar to me, but after a quick search, I found out they even make domestic appliances like LG and Samsung here. The information itself was reliable, and the technology was excellent! Considering the low price and the technology, I had to trust them to get my money's worth. The delivery/installation technician contacted me the next day after I ordered, requested photos of the installation location, and we coordinated the schedule. I was worried about installation delays because it was in the countryside, but thankfully, they installed it as quickly as possible to fit my schedule and were incredibly friendly. Depending on your kitchen, you may incur a small installation fee! We installed a built-in dishwasher, and there was some construction work involved, so we ended up paying around 30,000 won. However, they installed it quickly and even gave a quick demonstration and brief explanation! The product quality is so high-quality that my mom spends all day lounging around the dishwasher. First of all, I was very satisfied with the smooth installation. Just being satisfied with the installation isn't enough, right? I tried it right after dinner. 1. It saves time. First of all, it's amazing. I can use the dishwasher to do other things after it's done, which is great. My mom is the most satisfied! 2. I heard using the dishwasher actually minimizes water consumption? It's more environmentally friendly than washing dishes by hand! I tried it after making galbijjim (braised short ribs) and it removed all the grease very well! 3. Washing at high temperatures feels much more hygienic. The door automatically opens after washing, which is great for air drying. 4. The stainless steel interior is a plus! It's clean and feels even more hygienic. 5. It's not too noisy. I can run it in the kitchen and watch TV in the living room, and it doesn't even hear me! In fact, I can hear it the whole time. 6. I love the variety of modes. I only used it for 90 minutes, but there are seven different modes! I also love that the height can be adjusted. The user manual is very well written, so I plan to learn more as I use it. Above all, these specs for this price. It's crazy! This is a great buy. Everyone, get it!

Sentence (English): We purchased this to replace our Samsung Dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Great so far! ] || ---------------- || We purchased this to replace our Samsung Dishwasher. It was easy to follow the install, except our flooring in the kitchen is tile and drops down to cement under the dishwasher. Also we had a strip of wood parallel to our cabinets (to support the outter counter since the dishwasher is on the edge of our countertops so it was very difficult to slide it in, because we had to lift slide it in by proping up the back to slide on top of the wood. The only thing I would change is the way the legs individually adjust for height, our prior dishwasher had a screw in the front that you use an allen wrench to lower or make taller after you slide it in and the side did not come down so far by the legs so it was much easier to install. The other thing I wish it did is pop open after drying to help air dry which our old one did. With those 2 cons, the pros I liked is that it is much larger and I can fit more items inside. I feel like the brand will be better as far as customer service since, and the racks feel more sturdy than our older one. It runs very quiet and cleans very well. I feel like I chose a good model and I like the look. One concern I noted was some reviews I researched said the control panel on top started to bubble up/warp after a while. Hopefully, these were defective models, and our dishwasher lasts. Most other customer reviews had an overall high rating.

Sentence (English): Purchased from Home Depot with installation arranged by Home Deot through a third party contractor.
Comments (English): [ Great, with some caveats ] || ---------------- || Purchased from Home Depot with installation arranged by Home Deot through a third party contractor. Our first delivery was rejected by the installers after it failed to operate correctly on test. They uninstalled it and took it away again, telling us to contact HD for a replacement. That was fairly straight forward but the replacement shipped from Texas and we had ten days without a dishwasher and multiple house guests. For this price point would not expect a dud out of the box. Replacement machine operates flawlessly. 60 minute cycle gets most plastics totally dry. Auto plus crystal dry gets virtually everything perfect. I do notice that it is much no higher pressure than our v previous dishwasher, and it can flip lightweight plastic items. Love the third rack for cutlery. Yes, you can get perfect results with scraped only plates and messy cutlery. It is amazing! One thing I would change--if I did it again I would get the handle version not the pocket door. The pocket door ends up with lots of finger prints on the door

Sentence (English): I bought a Bosch after researching dishwashers.
Comments (English): [ Love it! ] || ---------------- || I bought a Bosch after researching dishwashers. I have had it for a couple of months and I love it so far. It is so quiet I can hardly tell it is on. Thank goodness they have a red light that lights up when it is on and shines on the floor. I hardly ever use drying modes because it dries everything really well without their use so far. I like not having to rinse my plates - I just wipe them out well (I have a septic tank and am very careful not to put anything down the drains)and load up the dishwasher in the evening. My dishes, glasses, and pots come out sparkling. I use the cleaning pods that were recommended and have virtually no streaks or spots. I also love the cutlery rack at the top. The racks can be adjusted to fit larger items in the dishwasher and that is a plus as well. I haven't cleaned the filter yet but I don't think I will have to do that very often. It is nice to know that there is a filter to catch particles that I might miss. The outside is easy to clean. I really love how quiet it is and how clean it gets my dishes. I would recommend it to anyone.

Sentence (English): A very practical dishwasher thanks to the dynamic layout of the baskets.
Comments (English): [ Practical, fast and large dishwasher ] || ---------------- || A very practical dishwasher thanks to the dynamic layout of the baskets. The cutlery drawer is fine, but a little less handy for thicker cutlery. The settings are very quick via the app, a little less quick via the control buttons. But setting a favourite is a great solution to start the dishwasher quickly. Even our children aged 2.5 and 4 can set up the dishwasher. A downside is that it does not automatically spring open at the end of the programme and that the LED indicator is on the side instead of shining on the floor.
Comments (Original): [ Praktische, snelle en grote vaatwasser ] || ---------------- || Een zeer praktische vaatwasser dankzij de dynamische indeling in de manden. De besteklade is prima, maar iets minder handig voor dikker bestek.De instellingen gaan heel vlot via de app, iets minder vlot via de bedieningsknoppen. Maar een favoriet instellen is een geweldige oplossing om de vaatwasser snel te starten. Zelfs onze kinderen van 2.5 en 4 kunnen de vaatwasser opzetten.Minpuntje is dat hij niet vanzelf open springt aan het einde van het programma en dat de led indicatie aan de zijkant zit ipv op de vloer schijnt.

It was the same guy from our first call that lectured us again about dishes sitting too long and rinse aid. (FYI - I had dishes sitting in the sink so that he would have a clean dishwasher to work with). After he was done lecturing us, he told us that the top water spinner needed to be replaced because the holes are clogged. As we are out of warranty, this is now a $270 cost on a dishwasher that has been flaky on cleaning since we got it. As much as we love the aesthetics of it - that Matte White and Bronze is beautiful - a pricepoint this high for a non-performing dishwasher and the costs we now have to sink into this a year and a half later dont make it worth it. The top rack for small dishes and cups/mugs has similar issues. Now I did notice a friend got a new Bosch, same design as mine and they have reconfigured the bottom rack so maybe they've listened to customer reviews. Very disappointed in the ability to fit dishes on top and bottom rack. Now that they've redesigned the bottom rack, I'm wondering if I could just order a new one. Love the silverware drawer at the top. I also find that even though my dishwasher is usually only half- 3/4s full that it doesn't really wash well unless I use the auto or normal cycles which are over 2 hours.

Sentence (English): I wanted to wait a bit to see how things went with this before reviewing.
Comments (English): [ So very quiet, cleanest dishes ] || ---------------- || I wanted to wait a bit to see how things went with this before reviewing. It has been through about a dozen loads now. PRO1. There is a lot of room. I haven't' tried to do a half bakers sheet or any of my commercial pots in it yet. The 2nd rack isn't removal so I'm thinking that the 60qt pots won't fit, the 40qt will for sure. 2. It is so quiet I keep trying to open it to see if it's running. I can barely hear it, unless it is draining, then the sink drain trap doesn't cover the noise of that, but I never heard it on my 20 year old GE before. Seriously you can't hear it run. That is awesome. 3. The top door controls are slick, it gives it such a neat sleek appearance, and I really like that. 4. Options, options, options! I am a bachelor so rinse and hold is great. I have only used the hi temp settings once, it didn't' melt anything. The heated dry works well, it won't get the pooled-up water on top of Tupperware and such. Seriously could get by with just express wash but sometimes my pots and pans need the pro wash feature. I wish there was a china feature as I have expensive wine goblets and depression glass. I was skeptical of the top rack for silverware at first, but now I am sold on it (see my Cons comment on silverware)5. There isn't a bunch of residue on my dishes. The filter screen is easy to remove and clean. I just scrape, light rinse and load. Before I practically had to wash the dishes to "sanitize" them. 6. If you are replacing an undercounter dishwasher it's easy to install. You will need to re-use your parts from original and/or buy the installation kit. Some of which you won't use, or you might. I was leery of reusing the hi pressure fill hose, so I replaced it and used the existing drain hose and power cord. CON (as I see it) 1. The silverware basket is too large. It could be 1/2 to 3/4 that size with the top 3rd rack. I never fill them both or more than half way. 2. The middle rack is not removable as far as I can tell. (nor are any of them as far as I know) there is more room for taller objects on the bottom or middle both with it's adjustments. 3. While it has the nicest racks out of the dishwasher, they have more "heft" to them and don't feel lek they will fall apart. From what I looked at they are oddly spaced tines and nothing stops plates from sliding front to back when you push in rack. (I got these little purple silicon wine glass holders that slide onto the tines and stretch across the rack, they work great and hold your wine glasses in place also. 4 to make the tub as tall as they do, the door handle almost hits the floor to open fully and pull out the rack. It doesn't' hit, but close and is a strange adjustment. 5. The Insulation blanket on the bottom has a weird fit and I can't seem to get it adjusted to stay in place and not peek out from the cover panel. I'm old with bad knees and it's just hard to get it to fit right, there isn't a lot of wiggle room. 6 My biggest complaint is that the fill fitting for the high-pressure hose inlet is made of plastic and threads oddly. It never looks like the hose connector is fitted squarely. Very concerning, but it is tight and doesn't leek. I am concerned it could become a point of failure. Hopefully the drip pan and float switch work correctly if they are needed. Main deal, after looking over almost 40 dishwashers I settled on this, and I'd buy it again in a heart beat.

Sentence (English): I went with this model because of the high rating on Consumer Reports and I have to say there are a lot of pros regarding this model.
Comments (English): [ great but requires patience ] || ---------------- || I went with this model because of the high rating on Consumer Reports and I have to say there are a lot of pros regarding this model. I love the sleek front (not hard to clean areas, smooth front). After reading reviews of rust, I wipe it down and dry it every day - it's important to not let water sit on it. It is very easy to clean and no fingerprints are left on it. I love the top controls and the variety of settings. The machine is very quiet when running. The top rack is a really nice addition (great for water bottle lids, larger utensils, tupperware lids, etc.) but I am so happy it still has the utensil caddy on the lowest rack - lots of space for all the small stuff. CONS: The biggest con for me is the run time. I typically choose the "Sensor" setting with the sanitize option and the complete cycles take 4 hours and 13 mins. Being a family of 5 that is home majority of the time, we create a lot of dishes so I wish the run time was faster. There is a bit of water that does not dry at the end of the cycle. I always unload the top rack last because that one seems to have the most water laying on it. The bottom two racks are fairly dry. I have noticed if I crack the door once the cycle is complete, more drying takes place but again, longer down time between cycles. **Also, a helpful tip we received from the installer was to always use a dishwasher gel (no packs, no powders). It is the easiest on the machine. Powder tends to not fully dissolve and over time it coats the drains/holes and results in poor performance. Gel will extend the life of the machine. (Installer was great and very helpful. Went above and beyond! )

Sentence (English): I wanted to wait a bit to see how things went with this before reviewing.
Comments (English): [ So very quiet, cleanest dishes ] || ---------------- || I wanted to wait a bit to see how things went with this before reviewing. It has been through about a dozen loads now. PRO 1. There is a lot of room. I haven't' tried to do a half bakers sheet or any of my commercial pots in it yet. The 2nd rack isn't removal so I'm thinking that the 60qt pots won't fit, the 40qt will for sure. 2. It is so quiet I keep trying to open it to see if it's running. I can barely hear it, unless it is draining, then the sink drain trap doesn't cover the noise of that, but I never heard it on my 20 year old GE before. Seriously you can't hear it run. That is awesome. 3. The top door controls are slick, it gives it such a neat sleek appearance, and I really like that. 4. Options, options, options! I am a bachelor so rinse and hold is great. I have only used the hi temp settings once, it didn't' melt anything. The heated dry works well, it won't get the pooled-up water on top of Tupperware and such. Seriously could get by with just express wash but sometimes my pots and pans need the pro wash feature. I wish there was a china feature as I have expensive wine goblets and depression glass. I was skeptical of the top rack for silverware at first, but now I am sold on it (see my Cons comment on silverware) 5. There isn't a bunch of residue on my dishes. The filter screen is easy to remove and clean. I just scrape, light rinse and load. Before I practically had to wash the dishes to "sanitize" them. 6. If you are replacing an undercounter dishwasher it's easy to install. You will need to re-use your parts from original and/or buy the installation kit. Some of which you won't use, or you might. I was leery of reusing the hi pressure fill hose, so I replaced it and used the existing drain hose and power cord. CON (as I see it) 1. The silverware basket is too large. It could be 1/2 to 3/4 that size with the top 3rd rack. I never fill them both or more than half way. 2. The middle rack is not removable as far as I can tell. (nor are any of them as far as I know) there is more room for taller objects on the bottom or middle both with it's adjustments. 3. While it has the nicest racks out of the dishwasher, they have more "heft" to them and don't feel lek they will fall apart. From what I looked at they are oddly spaced tines and nothing stops plates from sliding front to back when you push in rack. (I got these little purple silicon wine glass holders that slide onto the tines and stretch across the rack, they work great and hold your wine glasses in place also. 4 to make the tub as tall as they do, the door handle almost hits the floor to open fully and pull out the rack. It doesn't' hit, but close and is a strange adjustment. 5. The Insulation blanket on the bottom has a weird fit and I can't seem to get it adjusted to stay in place and not peek out from the cover panel. I'm old with bad knees and it's just hard to get it to fit right, there isn't a lot of wiggle room. 6 My biggest complaint is that the fill fitting for the high-pressure hose inlet is made of plastic and threads oddly. It never looks like the hose connector is fitted squarely. Very concerning, but it is tight and doesn't leek. I am concerned it could become a point of failure. Hopefully the drip pan and float switch work correctly if they are needed. Main deal, after looking over almost 40 dishwashers I settled on this, and I'd buy it again in a heart beat.

I can barely hear it, unless it is draining, then the sink drain trap doesn't cover the noise of that, but I never heard it on my 20 year old GE before. Seriously you can't hear it run. That is awesome. 3. The top door controls are slick, it gives it such a neat sleek appearance, and I really like that. 4. Options, options, options! I am a bachelor so rinse and hold is great. If you are replacing an undercounter dishwasher it's easy to install. You will need to re-use your parts from original and/or buy the installation kit. Some of which you won't use, or you might. (nor are any of them as far as I know) there is more room for taller objects on the bottom or middle both with it's adjustments. 3. While it has the nicest racks out of the dishwasher, they have more "heft" to them and don't feel lek they will fall apart. So if the install is right next to the sink, and you are not very careful, you can scrape your leg pretty bad even with a small rub against the open dishwasher door.

So if the install is right next to the sink, and you are not very careful, you can scrape your leg pretty bad even with a small rub against the open dishwasher door.
